# Add regression guard test for scaffold scripts

## Summary

Add `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts` to assert that no `scaffold:game` or `scaffold:games` keys are declared in `package.json`, and that every `scaffold*` script's target file exists on disk.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts` exists and is collected by the existing `unit` project (via `tests/**/*.test.ts` glob).
2. The test reads `package.json` and asserts `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` are **not** present in `scripts`.
3. The test iterates all keys matching `scaffold*` in `scripts`, resolves each command to a file path, and asserts the file exists.
4. `npm test` (vitest) passes with this new test included.

## Dependencies

None (runs against the live repo state).

## Deliverables

- `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts`
data.title: Add regression guard test for scaffold scripts

# Remove broken scaffold:game(s) from root package.json

## Summary

Hand-edit the root `package.json` to remove the two broken npm scripts `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` (which point at a non-existent `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` in this repo). Preserve the working `scaffold` script pointing at `./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `package.json` no longer declares `scaffold:game` or `scaffold:games` in `scripts`.
2. `package.json` still declares `scaffold` with value `tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street --game-repo-root . --core-root ./core`.
3. No other scripts in `package.json` are removed or altered.
4. The regression guard test (`tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts`) passes.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: "Add regression guard test for scaffold scripts" (the test must exist first, test-first ordering).

## Constraints

- Must be a **hand edit** — running `npm run scaffold` against the live checkout would drop 10 locally-added scripts (see item Constraints).

## Deliverables

- Edited `package.json`

# Filter core-only scaffold scripts in renderPackageJson

## Summary

In the **Tableau-Card-Engine** repo, modify `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` `renderPackageJson` to filter the core-only `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` entries out of the inherited scripts map, so the generated game-repo `package.json` no longer emits them.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `renderPackageJson` accepts a core manifest whose `scripts` map includes `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games`, and the rendered game-repo `package.json` omits both keys.
2. The filter is a small, explicitly-named drop-list (or drops any inherited script referencing the core-only `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` target), with a comment explaining the Option C no-root-`scripts/` rationale and pointing at the follow-up item for the broader class.
3. Existing `renderPackageJson` behaviour is otherwise unchanged (inherited scripts still pass through except the two dropped keys).
4. The change lands in the Tableau-Card-Engine repo on `dev` (CG work item) and is merged.

## Dependencies

Blocked by: "Add template omission unit test" (test-first).

## Deliverables

- Changed `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` in Tableau-Card-Engine

# Improved activity log — filter by player / AI / all

## Problem statement

In competitive (human-vs-AI) play the Activity Log mixes the human seat's
actions, every AI seat's actions and shared turn/world events into one
undifferentiated stream, so a player cannot follow their own story or an
opponent's without reading every line. The log needs simple filter controls so
the player can view all activity, only their own activity, or only AI activity.

## Users

- **Competitive player** — wants to review what they did this game without
  wading through AI turns.
- **Competitive player** — wants to study an AI opponent's behaviour to learn
  from it.
- **Single-player / tutorial player** — must see an unchanged log; there is no
  AI seat to filter, so the controls must not appear.

Example user stories:

- As a competitive player, I want to show only my own activity so I can review
  my spending and income this game.
- As a competitive player, I want to show only AI activity so I can see how an
  opponent is building their street.
- As a competitive player, I want to return to the full log with one click so I
  can see the whole game in context.
- As a single-player player, I want the log to look and behave exactly as it
  does today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In competitive mode the Activity Log panel presents three mutually exclusive
  filter controls — **All** (default), **You**, **AI** — and the active control
  is visually distinguishable from the inactive controls by more than colour
  alone (fill/stroke/text treatment).
- Selecting a filter re-renders the log to show only entries matching that
  filter, **without** mutating `state.activityLog`, changing entry order, or
  altering the persisted save data. Filtering is presentation-only.
- **Attribution is complete enough for the filter to be truthful**: every
  entry created by an acting seat's action (purchase, sell, upgrade, event play,
  hire, loan, income, reputation, etc.) is attributed to that seat, so
  filtering by You/AI never silently drops or mislabels a seat action.
- Turn headers and shared/turn-level entries (per-turn net summary, incident,
  market refresh/deal-in, week start, game-over) remain visible under every
  filter so turn structure and shared world events are never lost. A filter
  with no matching entries shows a clear, non-blank empty-state line.
- The filter controls are hidden and the log renders unchanged in
  single-player and tutorial modes; the selected filter survives turn end and
  UI refresh within a session and resets to **All** on scene restart / new game
  (never persisted to save data).
- Automated tests cover the pure filter/attribution predicate and the browser
  rendering: each filter shows exactly the expected entries, attribution is
  asserted for every action path, an empty filter shows the empty-state line,
  and no entry is lost or duplicated.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
  (`docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`,
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Presentation-only** — filtering must never mutate game state, consume RNG,
  or change transcript/replay output (`state.activityLog` is read-only during
  render).
- **Single-player and tutorial are byte-for-byte unchanged** — no controls, no
  attribution, no seat prefixes (existing precedent: `resolveLogSeatColour`,
  `getSeatDisplayLabel` no-op with no roster or one seat).
- **Preserve the existing Activity Log contracts**: deferred-render ordering
  (`logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`, MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2), scene-creation reset
  (MS-0MV14JDUG000E1V6), auto-scroll/no-yank behaviour, word-wrap and the
  per-entry visibility optimisation.
- **Positioning follows the SLL layout authority** (`src/layouts/main-street.layout.json`,
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`); the `activityLog` zone is
  ~300 × 218 px with a 22 px title bar, so the control treatment must fit
  without clipping or hiding the newest entry.
- **Colour is never the sole carrier of meaning** — the active filter must be
  readable without colour perception (text/fill/stroke differences).
- Reuse the shared `createActionButton` helper from `@ui/Renderer`; no new core
  engine infrastructure.
- Keep the change surgical: per-seat filters, type filters (gain/loss),
  filter persistence and a Settings toggle are **out of scope** (record them as
  linked follow-ups if they come up).

## Existing state

- `MainStreetState.activityLog: LogEntry[]` — each entry has `turn`, `text`,
  `type` (`gain` | `loss` | `neutral` | `turn-header`) and, in competitive mode,
  optional `seatId` / `seatLabel` / `seatColour`
  (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`).
- `refreshLog()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts`) renders **all**
  entries into `logContentContainer`, applies per-entry visibility, recomputes
  `logTotalContentH` / `logMaxScroll` and honours the deferral gate and
  auto-scroll.
- The panel is built once in `createContainers` (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`):
  `logContainer` → title bar (`'Activity Log'`, `LOG_TITLE_H = 22`) →
  `logContentContainer` → renderer-aware clip → wheel scroll.
- **Seat attribution is currently partial.** Only per-seat income/reputation
  entries use the seat overload `addLog(state, seatId, text, type)`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`). Most action entries (purchases, sells,
  upgrades, event plays, hires, loans) call the shared overload
  `addLog(state, text, type)` in `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`,
  `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`, etc., and
  therefore carry no `seatId`.
- Competitive mode is detected by the presence of `state.players` (absent in
  single-player); seat 0 controls the human (`controller === 'human'`, resolved
  by `findHumanSeatId`), every other seat is an AI (`AI 1`, `AI 2`, …).
- There is **no filter state** in the scene or the save shape today.

## Desired change

1. Add a presentation-only `logFilter` (`'all' | 'human' | 'ai'`) to the scene,
   defaulting to `'all'` and reset on scene creation.
2. Extend seat attribution so every entry produced by an acting seat's action
   carries that seat (`seatId` / `seatLabel` / `seatColour`); genuinely shared
   and turn-level entries stay unattributed.
3. Add three persistent filter controls to the Activity Log panel (compact row
   beneath the title bar), showing the active selection.
4. Filter the entry list in `refreshLog()` before rendering, recomputing content
   height and scroll bounds; keep shared/turn-level entries visible; show an
   empty-state line when a filter matches nothing.
5. Hide the controls (and render unchanged) when fewer than two seats exist
   (single-player / tutorial).
6. Cover the predicate, attribution and rendering with automated tests and
   update the docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — build the persistent filter
  controls inside the Activity Log panel (row under the title bar).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — filter entries in `refreshLog()`,
  recompute total content height/scroll bounds, empty-state line, ignore
  filtered-out entries in visibility and auto-scroll.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `logFilter` field (+ reset on scene
  creation) and any filter-control bookkeeping.
- `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` — shared seat-attribution helper / overload used
  by action paths; keep the prefix legibility contract.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `LogFilter` type and any attribution fields.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`,
  `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`,
  `src/MainStreetLoans.ts`, `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — stamp the acting
  seat on action entries.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — filter-row height / control constants
  (derived from the SLL panel width, not hard-coded panel coordinates).
- `src/MainStreetLogFilter.ts` — pure filter predicate module (`LogFilter`,
  predicate, control-visibility helper).
- `tests/main-street/helpers/activity-log-harness.ts` — shared headless action
  driver and competitive scene boot helper.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-filter.test.ts` — pure filter predicate and
  attribution coverage.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-filter.browser.test.ts` — rendering: each
  filter, empty state, single-player/tutorial unchanged, scroll bounds.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — Activity Log section: filtering and
  attribution.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — panel/control treatment notes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Attribution gap is the top risk.** If only per-seat income entries are
  attributed, a "You"/"AI" filter would hide most real actions and be
  misleading. **Producer confirmed (Q1 = A):** attribution is extended to all
  acting-seat entries before the filter ships, with tests on every action path.
- **Layout pressure.** The panel is 300 px wide with a 22 px title bar; a
  filter row reduces visible log height. Mitigation: derive the filter-row
  height from a constant and subtract it from `visibleH` so scroll bounds stay
  correct.
- **Deferred render interaction.** Filter changes made during end-of-turn
  deferral must apply on the next render, not force a render that violates the
  ordering contract.
- **Auto-scroll interaction.** A filter change alters max scroll; clamp the
  offset and preserve the player's "scrolled up" position, otherwise focus
  jumps unexpectedly.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Per-seat (AI 1 / AI 2) filtering, gain/loss type
  filters, persisting the filter across sessions and a Settings toggle are
  deliberately excluded; record them as linked follow-up work items rather than
  widening this item.
- **Assumption A (granularity).** "Player or AI ... all together" is
  interpreted as three buckets: **All / You / AI**, where "AI" groups every AI
  seat. Per-seat filtering is a separate future item.
- **Assumption B (persistence).** The selected filter lives in scene state
  only: it survives turns and UI refreshes, resets to **All** on scene
  restart / new game, and is not serialised into save data.
- **Assumption C (placement).** The controls are a compact row immediately
  beneath the existing title bar; the title text and title height are unchanged.
- **Assumption D.** The tutorial's existing highlight/hit-area expectations are
  preserved because the controls are hidden while the tutorial is active.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF** — Identify different AI players (completed): added the
  seat label/colour prefix to log entries (`resolveLogSeatColour`,
  `getSeatDisplayLabel`), the attribution foundation this filter builds on.
- **MS-0MV14JDUG000E1V6** — Turn log no longer displays (completed): the log
  content regression and its scene-creation reset contract that must not
  regress.
- **MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2** — Activity Log should not show log line until the
  results have been shown in the UI (completed): the deferred-render ordering
  contract that filtering must respect.
- **MS-0MV1BMMO900824N9** — Restore Activity Log rendering (completed):
  `refreshLog` deferral gate and count-based re-render; filtering changes the
  re-render trigger, so this contract is in scope.
- **MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP** — Playable AI competitive mode (human vs AI)
  (completed): the mode in which the filter is visible and meaningful.
- Related docs: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (Activity Log section),
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (play-panel treatment and seat colours).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

### Q1 — Attribution completeness

**Question:** Today only per-seat income/reputation entries carry a seat; most
play actions (purchases, sells, upgrades, event plays, hires, loans) are
unattributed. Should this item extend attribution so every acting-seat action
is stamped with that seat?

- (A) Yes — stamp the acting seat on all seat-action entries, then filter on
  complete attribution. *(Recommended)*
- (B) No — filter on the existing partial attribution only (accept that the
  filter will hide most player/AI actions).
- (C) Defer attribution to a separate blocking work item and land the filter
  afterwards.

**Recommended:** (A) — without complete attribution the filter is misleading and
would hide the very actions the player wants to review.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): (A)** — extend attribution so every
acting-seat action is stamped with that seat. Source: producer reply to the
intake questions comment (`MS-C0MW3GO7A4005DYW8`).

### Q2 — Shared / unattributed entries under a filter

**Question:** What should happen to entries with no seat (turn headers, per-turn
net summary, incidents, market refresh, week start, game-over) when **You** or
**AI** is selected?

- (A) Always show them under every filter. *(Recommended)*
- (B) Hide them unless **All** is selected.
- (C) Show only turn headers and the per-turn net summary, hiding shared world
  events (incidents, market refresh).

**Recommended:** (A) — turn structure and shared world events affect every seat
and keep the filtered log readable.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): (A)** — shared/turn-level entries (turn
headers, per-turn net summary, incidents, market refresh, week start,
game-over) stay visible under every filter. Source: producer reply to the
intake questions comment (`MS-C0MW3GO7A4005DYW8`).

### Q3 — Mode scope

**Question:** Single-player has no AI seats and no seat attribution. Should the
filter controls appear only in competitive mode?

- (A) Competitive only — hide the controls in single-player and tutorial and
  render the log unchanged. *(Recommended)*
- (B) All modes — show the controls everywhere (in single-player "AI" would be
  empty or undefined).
- (C) Single-player + competitive, hide only in the tutorial.

**Recommended:** (A) — there is nothing to filter without AI seats, and
single-player visuals stay unchanged.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): (A)** — controls appear in competitive mode
only; single-player and tutorial render the log unchanged. Source: producer
reply to the intake questions comment (`MS-C0MW3GO7A4005DYW8`).

### Documented assumptions (non-blocking)

- **Assumption A (granularity)** — All / You / AI, with AI grouping every AI
  seat. Source: the item description ("player or ai, or ... all together").
- **Assumption B (persistence)** — session-only filter state; reset to All on
  scene restart / new game; not saved.
- **Assumption C (placement)** — compact filter row beneath the existing title
  bar, preserving the title text and height.
- **Assumption D (tutorial)** — controls hidden while the tutorial is active,
  preserving tutorial highlight/hit-area expectations.

### Research summary

- Read `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` (`LogEntry`, `PlayerRecord`,
  `findHumanSeatId`), `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` (seat overload and prefix
  legibility), `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` (`refreshLog`, deferral
  gate, scroll bounds), `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` (panel
  construction) and `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` (SLL activityLog
  zone → 300 × 218).
- Audited every `addLog(` call site: 92 calls across 16 files; only
  `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` uses the seat overload for per-seat
  income/reputation. This is the evidence for the Q1 attribution gap.
- No filter state or filter UI exists in the scene, save shape or docs today;
  no duplicate or overlapping open work item was found.
- `find-related` automated report was run; its repo-file matches were
  `core/` docs with only generic keyword overlap and were not retained as
  related work.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MV1BMDU500878GN** – Add Activity Log regression test and pin introducing commit (completed)
- **MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2** – Activity Log should not show log line until the results have been showin in the UI (completed)
- **MS-0MV1BMMO900824N9** – Restore Activity Log rendering (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: activity, add, allows, buttons, filtering (+4 more)
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: activity, add, buttons, improved, log (+2 more)
- `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — matched: activity, add, buttons, filtering, log (+2 more)

# Engine DEVELOPER.md lists reduced motion among the paths that omit deferResourceApplication

Discovered from: MS-0MW20KSEG001DH1X (Turn summary dialog suppressed by reduced motion setting).

## Problem

`core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` (the Tableau-Card-Engine submodule), section *Deferred End-of-Turn Mutation* → bullet *Deferred `processEndOfTurn`*, says:

> Tutorial, reduced-motion and replay paths omit the flag (legacy immediate behaviour, no regression — AC5).

After MS-0MW20KSEG001DH1X the reduced-motion path does **not** omit the flag: the scene (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, `endTurn`) takes the deferred closing path under reduced motion, so the Turn Summary dialog has a `requiresDeferredClosing` result to gate on. Only the tutorial and replay paths still omit it.

## Why it was not fixed in the MS session

- `core` is a git submodule (a separate repository, detached HEAD at the engine pin `5a16c2f`). A working-tree edit leaves the submodule dirty, and `npm run build` runs `engine:sync` (non-soft), which **refuses** to sync a dirty submodule ("never clobber") — every later build in this repo would fail.
- A local commit inside the submodule is discarded by the next `engine:sync` (it checks out the remote target), so the fix would silently vanish.
- The engine checkout has no worklog (`wl` there reports "not initialized"), and pushing to the engine repo's `dev` is not authorised from a game-repo session.

## Fix

In the Tableau-Card-Engine repository, amend that bullet so only the tutorial and replay paths are named as flag-omitting, and state that the reduced-motion path takes the deferred closing so a game's Turn Summary gate can present its summary dialog (cross-reference the game-side behaviour).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` no longer claims the reduced-motion path omits `deferResourceApplication`.
2. The bullet names the tutorial and replay paths as the immediate/flag-omitting ones and explains why the reduced-motion path is deferred.
3. No code change is required; the engine's documentation guards (if any) still pass.

## Goal

Make specialization skills type-consistent, as recorded in the follow-up section of `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` (child of the Staff impact epic MS-0MW20VBSZ003A01O).

## Problem

`assignStaffApplicantSkills` gives every staff card 1–3 skills from the global pool regardless of the card's staff type, and the street-wide folds (`getEmployedSpecializationSkills`) aggregate every employed member's skills. A **business-staff** member can therefore hold a **management-company-scope** skill (Cost Cutter, Negotiator, Brand Ambassador, the four incident-mitigation skills, the Town Gossip baseline) and leak a player/street-scope effect, and a **management-company** member can draw business-scope skills (Chef, DJ, Networker, …) that can never resolve.

## Scope

1. **Scope gate (behavioural).** Apply player/street-scope effects only from management-company members and per-business effects only from the employing business's members, so a skill is inert when its scope does not match its holder's type. Keep the Operations Manager salary discount as a business-staff effect.
2. **Type-consistent assignment (deterministic).** Draw business-scope skills for business staff and player-scope skills for management-company staff, keeping the Town Gossip baseline on management-company cards. This changes the seeded assignment stream, so add determinism tests (same seed ⇒ same assignments).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Scope gate: a business-staff member holding Cost Cutter / Negotiator / Brand Ambassador / an incident-mitigation skill / the Town Gossip baseline produces no player- or street-scope effect, and a management-company member holding a business-scope skill produces no per-business buff.
2. Type-consistent assignment: business staff draw only business-scope skills; management-company staff draw only player-scope skills plus the Town Gossip baseline.
3. Determinism preserved: the assignment stream stays seeded and reproducible; existing determinism tests pass.
4. `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` follow-up section is updated to record that the gap is closed (or removed), and the GDD D.4.8 / card-catalog cross-references stay consistent.
5. Full test suite passes.

**Key Files:**
- src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts
- src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts
- src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts
- src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts
- docs/game/specialization-skills.md

Discovered during MS-0MW2XMB0P002D95K.

# Attribute every acting-seat action

## Goal

As a competitive player, I want every action I take and every action an AI seat
takes to be attributed to that seat in the Activity Log, so a You/AI filter is
truthful and never hides or mislabels a seat's action (producer decision Q1 =
A on MS-0MW1ZGM1F0010DQW).

## Acceptance Criteria

- In competitive mode (2+ seats), **attribution is complete enough for the
  filter to be truthful**: every entry created by an acting seat's action
  (purchase, sell, upgrade, event play, hire, loan, income, reputation) is
  attributed to that seat, so filtering by You or AI never silently drops or
  mislabels a seat action. The covered paths are buy-business,
  play-business-from-hand, buy-and-place, play-event, move-to-hand, upgrade
  (applied/played), hire staff, loan/bailout, income collection, reputation
  change and challenge/incident outcomes resolved by that seat — each entry
  carries `seatId`, `seatLabel` and `seatColour`.
- Genuinely shared / turn-level entries stay **unattributed**: turn header,
  per-turn net summary (`appendTurnNetRow`), incident, market refresh/deal-in,
  week start, game-over, and any tutorial/help line.
- Single-player and single-seat / tutorial games are unchanged: no seat fields
  are stamped, entry text is byte-identical, no prefix is drawn (existing
  `log-seat-prefix` and `activity-log-rendering` tests stay green).
- The attribution decision is **explicit at the call site**, not implicit: a
  shared/turn-level entry opts out through a named helper/overload flag, and the
  seat path derives the seat from the engine's acting-seat source
  (`state.activePlayerId`, falling back to no attribution when absent) rather
  than from UI state.
- Automated tests (extending `tests/main-street/activity-log-filter.test.ts`
  and its harness) assert attribution for **every** action path and the absence
  of attribution for **every** shared path — a single table-driven case per
  path, asserting `seatId`/`seatLabel`/`seatColour`.
- Undo/redo and replay paths do not double-stamp, drop or mislabel seat
  attribution; the finding (and any guard added) is recorded in a work-item
  comment.
- Changed-scope test gate passes via the test skill.

## Implementation

1. Decide the attribution seam (see Open Question): preferred is a single
   evaluated seam in `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` — the plain
   `addLog(state, text, type)` gets an explicit shared opt-out (e.g.
   `addLogShared(state, text, type)` or an `options.shared` flag) and the
   seat-ful path stamps `state.activePlayerId` when the roster has 2+ seats.
   Alternative: thread the acting seat through each action function.
2. Convert the shared call sites that are genuinely shared/turn-level to the
   named opt-out; leave acting-seat action call sites on the attributed path.
3. Keep `resolveLogSeatColour` / `getSeatDisplayLabel` as the single legibility
   and label source (no new palette or label logic).
4. Add the attribution test table; assert both the positive (attributed) and
   negative (shared) cases.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStateLog.ts` — attribution seam and shared opt-out.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `LogEntry` seat fields (already present).
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — action command log sites.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — purchase / upgrade / hire log sites.
- `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts` — sell log sites.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — turn header, net summary, incident,
  game-over log sites (shared opt-out).
- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — loan / bailout log sites.
- `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — challenge outcome log sites.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — existing per-seat income/reputation
  overload (must keep working through the new seam).
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-filter.test.ts` — attribution table.
- `tests/main-street/helpers/activity-log-harness.ts` — action driver
  (created by the harness child).

## Open Questions

- **OPEN QUESTION (implementer, non-blocking):** confirm the attribution seam —
  centralise it in `addLog` (deriving the seat from `state.activePlayerId`, with
  an explicit shared opt-out) versus threading the acting seat through each
  action function. Evidence required: replay-mode and undo/redo paths must keep
  attribution correct; record the finding in a work-item comment.

## Notes

- Risk: entries appended while `activePlayerId` is a different seat (deferred
  turn closing, AI simulation loops, replay mode). Where the ambient seat is not
  the acting seat, pass the seat explicitly instead of relying on the default.
- Scope guard: per-seat filters, gain/loss type filters and persisting
  attribution in new save fields are out of scope.
data.title: Seat attribution for every action

# Scene filter state and filtered rendering

## Goal

As a competitive player, I want the Activity Log to render only the entries
matching the selected filter (while keeping turn structure and shared world
events visible), so I can read my own story or an opponent's without wading
through every line.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `logFilter: LogFilter` exists as scene state, defaults to `'all'`, is reset in
  the scene-creation log-reset block (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle`) and
  is **never** written to save data (a round-trip test asserts the serialised
  state contains no `logFilter`).
- Selecting a filter re-renders the log to show only entries matching that
  filter, **without** mutating `state.activityLog`, changing entry order or
  altering the persisted save data — filtering is presentation-only; a
  deep-clone comparison asserts the entries array is untouched and the render
  goes through the pure predicate.
- Content height (`logTotalContentH`), `logMaxScroll` and `logScrollOffset` are
  recomputed from the **rendered** entries only, and the visible height accounts
  for the filter-row height constant so scroll bounds stay correct.
- Auto-scroll contract preserved: when the reader was at the bottom the view
  stays at the bottom after a filter change; when scrolled up the offset is
  clamped (never yanked to the bottom, never left past the new `logMaxScroll`).
- Turn headers and shared/turn-level entries (per-turn net summary, incident,
  market refresh/deal-in, week start, game-over) remain visible under every
  filter so turn structure and shared world events are never lost; a filter
  with no matching entries (even shared ones) shows a clear, non-blank
  empty-state line (`No activity for this filter`).
- Deferred-render contract preserved (`logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`):
  filtering during deferral applies on the next render and never forces a render
  out of order; a filter change is a re-render trigger even when the entry count
  is unchanged (tracked alongside `logPrevEntryCount`).
- The per-entry visibility pass only considers rendered entries, and no entry is
  lost or duplicated across filters.
- Browser tests cover: each filter renders exactly the expected entries (You /
  AI / shared / turn headers), empty state line, scroll bounds and clamping,
  deferred filter change, and save round-trip without `logFilter`.
- Automated tests cover the pure filter and attribution predicate and the
  browser rendering: each filter shows exactly the expected entries,
  attribution is asserted for every action path, an empty filter shows the
  empty-state line, and no entry is lost or duplicated.
- Changed-scope test gate passes via the test skill.

## Implementation

1. Add `logFilter` to the scene plus its reset in the lifecycle reset block.
2. In `refreshLog()`, derive `visibleEntries = filterLogEntries(activityLog,
   logFilter, humanSeatId)` before the render loop; use it for height,
   scroll bounds, the empty-state line and the visibility pass.
3. Add the re-render trigger for a filter change (stored previous filter).
4. Add the filter-row height constant and subtract it from `visibleH`.
5. Extend `activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts` /
   `activity-log-filter.browser.test.ts` with the cases above.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — `refreshLog()` filtering, bounds,
  empty state, re-render trigger.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `logFilter` field.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — reset on scene creation.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — filter-row height constant.
- `src/MainStreetLogFilter.ts` — predicate (previous child).
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-filter.browser.test.ts` — rendering cases.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-filter.test.ts` — save round-trip assertion.

## Notes

- Depends on the pure predicate child; the controls row is a separate child, so
  tests set `scene.logFilter` directly here.
- Preserve the comment/contract references already in `refreshLog`
  (MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2, MS-0MV14JDUG000E1V6, MS-0MV1BMMO900824N9): extend the
  comments with the filter rule rather than rewriting them.
data.title: Filtered Activity Log rendering

# Activity Log filter controls

## Goal

As a competitive player, I want three visible filter controls on the Activity
Log panel — All / You / AI — so I can switch the view with one click and always
see which filter is active.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In competitive mode (2+ seats) the Activity Log panel shows a compact control
  row immediately beneath the 22 px title bar with three mutually exclusive
  controls — `All` (default), `You`, `AI` — built with the shared
  `createActionButton` helper from `@ui/Renderer`, with a height/width derived
  from the SLL panel geometry (`s.layout.logW`) and a named constant (no
  hard-coded panel coordinates).
- In competitive mode the Activity Log panel presents three mutually exclusive
  filter controls — All (default), You, AI — and the active control is visually
  distinguishable from the inactive controls by more than colour alone: a
  distinct fill/alpha, stroke weight and label treatment (e.g. bold + bright
  label vs normal + dimmed label), asserted in tests by reading the button's
  fill/stroke/label style rather than by pixel colour.
- Clicking a control sets `scene.logFilter` and re-renders the log through
  `renderer.refreshLog()` (respecting the deferral gate); clicking the active
  control is a no-op that does not re-render or mutate state.
- The filter controls are hidden and the log renders unchanged in single-player
  and tutorial modes (they also consume no vertical log space there); the
  selected filter survives turn end and UI refresh within a session and resets
  to All on scene restart or new game (never persisted to save data).
- The filter row is destroyed and rebuilt safely on scene restart / new game
  (no orphaned game objects, no duplicate rows after `scene.restart()`).
- Layout: the row fits the ~300 x 218 px panel, the newest entry is not hidden
  or clipped by the row, and the row stays inside the panel bounds.
- Browser tests cover: controls present in competitive mode and absent in
  single-player/tutorial; default active = `All`; active styling differs from
  inactive beyond colour; clicking `You`/`AI`/`All` switches the rendered entry
  set; restart does not leak or duplicate controls.
- Changed-scope test gate passes via the test skill.

## Implementation

1. Create a `logFilterContainer` (or named equivalent) added to `logContainer`
   in `createContainers`, beneath the title bar; three `createActionButton`
   instances with widths distributed across `s.layout.logW`.
2. Wire click handlers to set `s.logFilter` and call `renderer.refreshLog()`;
   repaint the active/inactive treatment from the current `logFilter`.
3. Hide the container (and skip its height in `visibleH`) when
   `shouldShowLogFilterControls(state)` is false.
4. Destroy the row in the same teardown path as the other persistent panels so
   scene restart is clean.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — build the filter row in
  `createContainers` (the Activity Log panel is created there).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — filter row height / button sizing
  constants.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — `refreshLog()` re-render entry point
  used by the click handlers.
- `core/src/ui/Renderer/index.ts` — `createActionButton` options
  (read-only: fill/stroke/label styling and `height`).
- `src/MainStreetLogFilter.ts` — `shouldShowLogFilterControls`.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-filter.browser.test.ts` — control rendering
  and click behaviour.

## Notes

- Colour is never the sole carrier of meaning: the label text always names the
  filter, and the active state must also differ in fill/stroke/weight.
- Out of scope (record as a follow-up only if it comes up): per-seat controls
  (`AI 1`, `AI 2`), gain/loss type filters, persisting the filter, a Settings
  toggle.
- Depends on the filtered-rendering child so a click is observable end-to-end.

# Activity Log filter documentation

## Goal

As a maintainer or player reading the docs, I want the Activity Log filtering
and seat-attribution rules documented, so the behaviour is discoverable and the
presentation-only contracts are explicit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
  (`docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`).
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (Activity Log section) documents: the
  All / You / AI filter and its default, what each bucket matches (AI groups
  every AI seat), which entries stay visible under every filter (turn headers,
  per-turn net summary, incidents, market refresh/deal-in, week start,
  game-over), the empty-state line, competitive-only availability, and that the
  selection is session-only (reset to All on scene restart / new game, never
  saved).
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` documents the filter control treatment: the
  compact row beneath the title bar, the active/inactive treatment that does not
  rely on colour, and the space it takes from the log viewport.
- The documented attribution rule matches the implementation: which action
  entries are seat-attributed versus which genuinely shared entries are
  unattributed.
- Inline code comments in the predicate module, the attribution seam and
  `refreshLog()` explain the presentation-only contract and reference the
  preserved contracts (deferred render MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2, scene reset
  MS-0MV14JDUG000E1V6, activity-log rendering MS-0MV1BMMO900824N9).
- Documentation names match the code: `logFilter`, `LogFilter`,
  `'all' | 'human' | 'ai'`, `shouldShowLogFilterControls`.
- README needs no change unless it describes the Activity Log — verified and

## Implementation

vertical slices (each child carries code + tests; the docs child carries the
full-suite gate). No producer questions were needed: the intake Appendix on
this item already answers Q1 (full seat attribution), Q2 (shared entries stay
visible) and Q3 (competitive mode only), and Assumptions A–D were accepted.

## Features (implementation order)

| # | Child | Type | Parent ACs covered |
|---|-------|------|--------------------|
| 1 | Activity Log filter acceptance harness (MS-0MW3PFLDP000CF2X) | task | test foundation |
| 2 | Seat attribution for every action (MS-0MW3PFQ4L0046Q3K) | feature | attribution AC |
